subject: Clarify DPA boundary: edge-proxy subprocessor, telemetry minimization, and transfer controls
messages:
From: Caroline Wu <caroline.wu@medflow.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medflow.ai
Date: 2026-07-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial SSQ + question on edge proxy subprocessor

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks for sending the initial security questionnaire. We reviewed the SSQ and had two quick asks before we route this to our legal/procurement team:

1) Edge-proxy vendor: your SSQ mentions an optional edge proxy (third-party vendor). Does the proxy ever receive PII payloads or only connection/metadata? We need to be clear for our DPA annexing (we carve subprocessors differently if they touch PII).

2) Telemetry minimization: we require a short statement on what telemetry you collect from calls routed through the proxy (fields, retention windows, encryption in transit). Any short bullet list will help us close the loop.

We can share the DPA annex template once we confirm the above so legal can draft the carveout language.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is hoping to get everything bundled by next Wednesday.

Cheers,
Caroline Wu
Head of Integrations | MedFlow AI
caroline.wu@medflow.ai

Attachments referenced: medflow_ssq_template.pdf (sent separately)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Caroline Wu <caroline.wu@medflow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-13T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SSQ + question on edge proxy subprocessor

On Tue, Jul 13, 2026 at 9:12 AM Caroline Wu <caroline.wu@medflow.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for sending the initial security questionnaire...

Hi Caroline — thanks for the note. Quick answers and next steps:

- Edge proxy scope: the optional edge proxy (TrustVault) is used only for connection brokering and DDoS mitigation at the network level. It does NOT persist customer PII. By design we configure the proxy to strip request bodies for routes that include identifiable fields; only connection metadata, TLS handshake info, and ephemeral session tokens are passed.

- Telemetry we collect (when proxy enabled):
  - connection_timestamp (ISO8601) — retained 14 days
  - source_ip (anonymized / CIDR-ified at 24h if requested)
  - latency_ms per request
  - status_code
  - ephemeral_session_token_id (no user payload)

We can provide a short attestation from the proxy vendor confirming no PII retention and a diagram showing the point where bodies are stripped. I'm attaching a redline of the DPA annex (dpa_annex_redline_v1.docx) with a suggested carveout: proxy allowed only for connection/metadata routing and explicit ban on payload persistence.

Next steps:
- I'll ask TrustVault to provide their short attestation and SOC timeline.
- Marissa / Olga: can you confirm whether we can add a 'no-export' optional clause for EU customers (Caroline, if you need that, let us know).

Happy to jump on a 30-minute sync if that helps.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Technical Sales 
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachments: dpa_annex_redline_v1.docx

From: David Liao <david.liao@trustvault.com>
To: Caroline Wu <caroline.wu@medflow.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-13T14:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SSQ + question on edge proxy subprocessor

Hi all — David from TrustVault here. Jonas asked me to chime in with the vendor perspective. Short answers:

- Data scope: TrustVault operates as an edge brokering service. We do not persist HTTP bodies for any Redwood routes configured with 'body_strip = true'. We retain ephemeral session tokens for up to 1 hour for connection re-use and then purge. We retain connection logs (timestamp, proxied_ip_cidr, status_code, latency_ms) for 14 days for incident investigation.

- PII handling: we never index or attempt to parse request payloads for PII by default. If a customer opts in to body analytics (not the default for Redwood customers), that would be treated as a separate service and contract.

- Evidence: attaching a short attestation (trustvault_attestation.pdf) and a pointer to our compliance page (SOC2: in progress, expected completion Q4 2026).

Jonas — on KMS custody: TrustVault does not hold customer KMS keys; any token encryption is performed with keys you manage (we integrate with customer KMS via an HSM-backed envelope pattern). If Redwood prefers, we can add a no-key-escrow clause to the DPA annex.

Happy to answer any follow-ups or join a call.

Best,
David Liao
TrustVault — Head of Product Security

Attachments: trustvault_attestation.pdf

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: compliance check + suggested clauses

Jonas / Marissa — internal note after reviewing David's attestation and our risk matrix:

- Positive: vendor confirms body stripping and no KMS custody; short retention windows are aligned with our standard.

- Risk items to add to redline before sending to MedFlow: 
  * Explicit ban on payload persistence by the proxy vendor (we already have wording but make it stronger — "no storage of request/response bodies beyond ephemeral buffering for immediate routing").
  * Add 'no-key-escrow' clause and a KMS custody exhibit: vendor must accept a technical attestation and demonstrate HSM integration.
  * Optional onshore processing carveout for EU customers or proof-of-onshore-workflow. For now mark as "requested for EU customers".

I've attached a brief (redwood_security_brief.pdf) with suggested language snippets we can push to legal. If MedFlow confirms EU residency is required, we'll propose a canary clause (onshore processing or geo-fencing by region).

Recommend we send an answer to MedFlow with: 1) TrustVault attestation, 2) updated DPA annex (stronger ban + KMS exhibit), 3) a redacted dataflow diagram link, and 4) proposed meeting times.

—Olga

Subject: Re: Clarify DPA boundary: edge-proxy subprocessor, telemetry minimization, and transfer controls

Caroline — thanks for the patience. Quick summary and concrete next steps so procurement can proceed: 

1) TrustVault scope: attached is their attestation confirming no PII persistence and the short retention windows (trustvault_attestation.pdf). They do not hold customer KMS keys and support an HSM-backed envelope pattern.

2) Telemetry: we will provide the following fields by default (retention 14 days): connection_timestamp, source_ip (anonymized on request), latency_ms, status_code, ephemeral_session_token_id (purged in 1 hour). We will add this short list to the DPA annex.

3) DPA annex: we attached our recommended redline (dpa_annex_redline_v1.docx) that:
   - Restricts the proxy to connection/metadata routing; explicitly prohibits payload storage beyond ephemeral buffering.
   - Adds a no-key-escrow clause and KMS custody exhibit language.
   - Includes an optional EU onshore processing carveout (mark as customer-selectable).

4) Dataflow diagram: redacted diagram available here — https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-dataflow-diagram-id (no customer identifiers).

5) Meeting: suggest a 30-minute call to walk legal/procurement through the redline and the attestation. Proposed slots (PDT): Thursday 7/16 10:00-10:30, 14:00-14:30. Please confirm.

If that looks good I'll ask legal to incorporate Olga's suggested stronger language before we send a final package.

Thanks,
